paper_sources_read.title: Recursive Language Models
paper_sources_read.abstract_excerpt: We study allowing large language models (LLMs) to process arbitrarily long prompts through the lens of inference-time scaling. We propose Recursive Language Models (RLMs), a general inference paradigm that treats long prompts as part of an external environment and allows the LLM to programmatically examine, decompose, and recursively call itself over snippets of the prompt. We find that RLMs can successfully process inputs up to two orders of magnitude beyond model context windows and, even for
mechanism_primitives: bounded recursive inspection of external context/state

aggregation of recursive sub-results into action or answer
learned policy for what to inspect, recurse on, and aggregate

paper_sources_read.title: iGRPO: Self-Feedback-Driven LLM Reasoning
paper_sources_read.abstract_excerpt: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise in solving complex mathematical problems, yet they still fall short of producing accurate and consistent solutions. Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a framework for aligning these models with task-specific rewards, improving overall quality and reliability. Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is an efficient, value-function-free alternative to Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) that leverages group-relative reward normalization. We introduce It
mechanism_primitives: sample multiple draft attempts under matched budget
condition refinement on the best scored draft
